message.content: I have annual revenue for FY2019–FY2025 (fiscal years ending Jan 31). Let me compute the year-over-year growth rates.

Snowflake Inc. (CIK 1640147) reported steadily growing total revenue every fiscal year, but the **growth rate decelerated sharply and consistently** over the period. Figures below use the consolidated `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` tag (USD, fiscal years ending January 31); growth rates are my calculations from those disclosed values.

| Fiscal year (end) | Revenue (USD) | YoY growth |
|---|---|---|
| FY2019 (2019-01-31) | 96.666M | — |
| FY2020 (2020-01-31) | 264.748M | +173.9% |
| FY2021 (2021-01-31) | 592.049M | +123.6% |
| FY2022 (2022-01-31) | 1,219.327M | +106.0% |
| FY2023 (2023-01-31) | 2,065.659M | +69.4% |
| FY2024 (2024-01-31) | 2,806.489M | +35.9% |
| FY2025 (2025-01-31) | 3,626.396M | +29.2% |

**Trend:** Revenue rose roughly 37-fold from FY2019 to FY2025, but the pace of growth fell in every year: from ~174% in FY2020 to ~29% in FY2025. The deceleration was steepest between FY2022 and FY2024 (106% → 69% → 36%), then moderated in FY2025, when growth eased only modestly (35.9% → 29.2%). This is the classic pattern of a high-growth company scaling off a much larger base.

**Sources (selected, latest applicable annual disclosure for each period):**
- FY2019: fact id 2509651, 10-K filed 2021-03-31, accession 0001640147-21-000073
- FY2020: fact id 2509655, 10-K filed 2022-03-30, accession 0001640147-22-000023
- FY2021: fact id 2509665, 10-K filed 2023-03-29, accession 0001640147-23-000030
- FY2022: fact id 2509678, 10-K filed 2024-03-26, accession 0001640147-24-000101
- FY2023: fact id 2509691, 10-K filed 2025-03-21, accession 0001640147-25-000052
- FY2024: fact id 2509703, 10-K filed 2025-03-21, accession 0001640147-25-000052
- FY2025: fact id 2509712, 10-K filed 2025-03-21, accession 0001640147-25-000052

**Notes/limitations:** These are total (consolidated) revenues; Snowflake also discloses product vs. services revenue, which I did not break out. The database also contains quarterly figures and later comparative restatements of the same annual periods; I used one value per fiscal year and did not sum duplicates. The FY2019 figure comes from a comparative column in the FY2021 10-K. The most recent annual report bundled is FY2025 (fiscal year ended 2025-01-31); partial FY2026 quarterly data exist but are not full-year figures.
